title: Choose the visual world for Redline
question: One world for both surfaces: the landing page and the app shell behind sign-in. Keep the roll, take the pick, adopt a challenger, or re-roll.

options.label: Duplicate Book
options.lineage: Carbonless duplicate order and invoice books, the kind every trade counter and back office keeps
options.thesis: Every flag is a carbon copy of the sentence it came from: the same words, pressed through.
materials: NCR carbonless sheets: white original, canary and pink copies
perforated tear lines and numbering-machine serials
options.viewport: An open duplicate book fills the screen: the white contract sheet on top, its renewal sentence pressed through onto a canary copy below as Flag No. 0001 with the tier box ticked, and a tear-off slip at the foot holding the upload and paste control.
options.risk: Tips into office-supply nostalgia if the copy colours go timid; carbon blue on pink needs checked contrast.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: the cited sentence sets large, labels small, no ornament.
One spot ink: serial-number red is the only emphasis colour, kept for the top tier and the action.
Fixed stations in printed order, like the book's numbered boxes: original, copy, tier, counter-offer.
An opened flag owns the whole sheet; the next flag waits one tear away.
Exposure is measured, never described: money, lock-in and notice in ruled boxes with tabular figures.
Each notice deadline is drawn as a perforation on the term line: the point where the buyer can no longer act.

regions.label: canary copy: Flag No. 0001, tier box

options.label: Exit Ahead
options.lineage: Interstate guide and warning signs: green panels, distance legends, yellow diamonds
options.thesis: Renewal and exit, signed like the road: every deadline a distance, every flag a sign you cannot miss.
materials: retroreflective sheeting on extruded aluminium panels
options.viewport: A green overhead gantry spans the top of the page with the sample contract's real terms as legends ('AUTO-RENEWAL 12 MONTHS', 'NOTICE 90 DAYS'); the contract sentence runs below like the road surface, and the action is the exit panel.
options.risk: The most familiar card here: wayfinding is a well-used metaphor and the exit pun can tip into cute.

regions.label: exit panel: try it on a document

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Drag an axis and the contract's sentences thicken by exposure.
options.viewport: One giant sentence with an exposure slider under it.
options.case: Buyers do not know type specimens, and a slider over the document reads as a toy: loses audience and clarity.
options.risk: Type-nerd world that hides the offer.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Flags develop out of the contract like a print in the tray.
options.viewport: A contract sheet emerging under amber light.
options.case: Slow emergence works against a tool that has to feel checked and immediate; no buyer recognises the room.
options.risk: Moody, dark and slow for a desk tool.

options.label: Magazine Program
options.lineage: mid-century magazine identity: serif grid, one spot colour per issue
options.thesis: Each analysis printed as an issue, with the flag as the cover story.
options.viewport: A serif masthead over a two-column contract read.
options.case: Editorial framing promises opinion, which Redline must never give; buyers do not identify with it.
options.kept: One spot ink carries all emphasis.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One flag per screen, snap to the next.
options.viewport: A single flag fills the viewport with actions on a right rail.
options.case: Familiar to buyers, but it tears flags away from the document, the one thing trust depends on.
options.kept: An opened flag owns the whole sheet.

options.label: Forge Floor
options.thesis: Each clause struck and measured under the hammer.
options.viewport: A glowing bar with clause figures chalked beside it.
options.case: Violence and heat misstate a calm reading tool; buyers do not see themselves at the anvil.
options.risk: Drama where clarity is the product.
options.kept: Measurements ruled in boxes with tabular figures.

options.label: Event Horizon
options.thesis: The renewal date as an event horizon you cannot come back from.
options.viewport: A ring of clauses orbiting a black centre.
options.case: Spectacle with no tie to the buyer's world, and it hides the sentence: loses both axes.
options.risk: Sci-fi costume on a contract tool.
options.kept: Mark the point of no return.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Legal-tech SaaS, executed impeccably: white ground, slate type, one blue.
materials: product screenshot in a browser frame
canonCard.viewport: Headline and upload button on the left, a screenshot of the flag list on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the tools Redline is meant to be more trustworthy than.
